subject: Verdance private deployment - urgent throughput drop and exec escalation
messages:
From: Ellen Moss <ellen@verdance.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden throughput collapse on our private cluster (p95 spikes, 502s)

Priyom,

We just hit a sharp degradation on our private VPC deployment in us-west-2. Over the last 10 minutes our p95 token latency jumped from ~180ms to ~1.6s and 502s climbed from <0.1% to ~7%. Traffic and request shape haven't changed on our side — same model version and traffic pattern. This is impacting our live inference and hitting SLAs.

Key notes:
- First observed at 09:02 PDT, sustained since ~09:05
- Multiple clients logging decode timeouts; sample traces attached (we'll share logs if needed)
- No config changes from Verdance in the last 24h

We need immediate remediation and an exec-level sync if this isn't resolved in the next 60 minutes. Please escalate to SRE and your engineering leadership.

Ellen Moss
Head of Platform
Verdance AI

Attachment: customer_metrics_0905.csv (attachment stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Moss <ellen@verdance.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-15T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse on our private cluster (p95 spikes, 502s)

Thanks Ellen — we see the same signal on our telemetry. I'm standing up a focused triage now and elevating to SRE and our account ops team.

Immediate next steps we are executing:
- Collecting perf dumps and decoder logs from your hot nodes (requesting an initial sample from your SRE team)
- Running a quick KV-cache / kernel-selection audit to rule out a runtime mismatch
- Applying an emergency concurrency cap to prevent queue amplification while we diagnose

I'll send a short internal note to loop in Marissa and Jonas and will get back within 20 minutes with the first findings. If this persists past 60 minutes I'll propose an exec sync.

— Priyom
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: initial-log-sample.json (attached by customer; referenced)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-15T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Verdance private cluster - urgent throughput investigation (triage)

Team — Ellen reported a rapid p95 jump and 7% 502s on Verdance's private VPC (us-west-2). Customer reports no config changes; traffic shape steady. Please treat as P1. Quick context and asks:

Observed signals (Redwood telemetry):
- p50 ~200ms, p95 ~1.6s, error-rate 502 ~7% beginning ~09:05 PDT
- Hot shard concentration on nodes n-03 and n-07 (KV cache miss rate increased)
- No immediate hardware alerts from fabric, but CPU NR utilization for decoders increased ~40% on hot nodes

Immediate investigative tasks:
1) Marissa - run a kernel-selection check and confirm quantized kernel compatibility for the currently pinned model (model id: rwd-nt-7b-v2). Check for mismatched kernels after last runtime hotfix.
2) Jonas - capture focused perf dumps from n-03/n-07, grab decoder stack traces, and validate network latency between shard owner and infer nodes. Prioritize perf_dump_0415.tar.gz format.
3) Laura - prepare a short exec note for the customer (CTO-level) if this is not resolved in 45 minutes. We'll need to justify a temporary capacity bump or fallback to a nearby region variant.

Mitigations we can push quickly:
- Soft cap concurrency on Verdance route to reduce queue amplification
- Force fallback to a lower-memory kernel on the hot nodes if kernel selection proves problematic
- Optional short-term warmup on cold nodes to rebalance KV cache

I'll coordinate with Verdance SRE for logs and give status updates every 20 minutes.

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Ellen Moss <ellen@verdance.ai>
Date: 2028-04-15T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Verdance private cluster - urgent throughput investigation (triage)

On Mon, Apr 15, 2028 at 09:37 Priyom Das wrote:
> Team — Ellen reported a rapid p95 jump and 7% 502s on Verdance's private VPC (us-west-2). Customer reports no config changes; traffic shape steady. Please treat as P1.

Status update and actions taken:
- Jonas and I validated the kernel selection logic. We observed that on n-03 the runtime selected an AVX2 float16 kernel path while the model had been recently applied with an int8-quant profile in the pinned-variant. This mismatched execution path caused increased decode CPU time and KV cache churn.
- Applied emergency mitigation: pinned runtime to the int8 kernel path on n-03 and n-07 and reapplied KV warmup hints. Early effect: p95 reduced from ~1.6s to ~620ms on the hot shard. Error rate dropped from 7% to ~1.9%.
- Collected perf dump and stack traces: attached perf_dump_0415.tar.gz. Also attached a quick remediation script (playbook_verdance_patch.sh) to automate kernel pinning for the rest of the cluster.

Further recommended steps (next 4 hours):
1) Full cluster rollout of the kernel pin (automated via playbook), with canary on 5% nodes first.
2) Run KV cache rewarm job during off-peak for hot shards and validate miss-rate trending down.
3) Post-mitigation, schedule a short postmortem to root-cause why the kernel-selection heuristic respected an older metadata tag.

Ellen — can your SRE confirm we've got permission to run the full playbook? If yes we can proceed with the canary rollout immediately.

Attachments: playbook_verdance_patch.sh, perf_dump_0415.tar.gz

— Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Moss <ellen@verdance.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Verdance private cluster - urgent throughput investigation (triage)

Ellen — quick summary and ask for exec sync:

What we saw:
- Root cause: kernel-selection mismatch on hot nodes caused high decode CPU and KV cache churn.
- Immediate impact: p95 from ~1.6s -> ~620ms after emergency kernel pin; 502s down from 7% -> ~1.9%.

What we did:
- Emergency kernel pin to int8 path on the two hot nodes; KV warm hint applied.
- Collected perf artifacts and prepared an automated playbook for canary rollout.

Recommended next steps:
- If you authorize the playbook, we'll run a 5% canary cluster rollout in the next 15 minutes and expand to full cluster over 45 minutes if green.
- Postmortem with timelines and a change to the kernel selection heuristic to validate model metadata at rollout time.
- Optional: a short capacity bump (temporary Dedicated capacity) for 2 hours if you want extra headroom during the rollout.

Request: please confirm we have permission to run the automated playbook (attached) so we can proceed with canary. If this is not sufficient please let me know whether to pull in your CTO for a 1pm PDT executive sync — we can make the time if you prefer an immediate leadership-level briefing.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — we'll continue to monitor and I'll post the canary result immediately.

— Priyom
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
